case_name: Full table scan — no WHERE clause
query: SELECT * FROM policy_data
problem: Entire table scanned with no filtering condition
root_cause: No WHERE clause forces the database to read all 10 million rows before returning results. No index can help.
suggestion: Always add a WHERE clause to limit rows. Add indexes on status, state, and created_date columns. Use LIMIT for exploratory queries.
fix_example: SELECT policy_id, status, state FROM policy_data WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' AND created_date >= '2024-01-01' LIMIT 100;

query: SELECT * FROM claims_data
problem: Full table scan on claims_data with no filtering
root_cause: SELECT * with no WHERE clause reads every row. Claims table has 8M rows causing very high I/O.
suggestion: Filter by claim_status, policy_id, or date range. Add composite index on (policy_id, claim_status).
fix_example: SELECT claim_id, policy_id, claim_amount FROM claims_data WHERE claim_status = 'PENDING' AND created_date > '2024-06-01';

query: SELECT * FROM large_transaction_table
problem: SELECT * fetches all columns unnecessarily, wasting bandwidth and memory
root_cause: Fetching all 40 columns when only 3 are needed. Extra data transfer slows network and memory.
suggestion: Specify only required columns. Avoid SELECT * in production code. Add covering index for frequently selected columns.
fix_example: SELECT transaction_id, amount, status FROM large_transaction_table WHERE status = 'PENDING';

query: UPDATE policy_data SET is_reviewed = 1
problem: UPDATE without WHERE clause modifies every row in the table
root_cause: Missing WHERE clause. All 10M rows locked and updated. Causes full table lock and massive undo log.
suggestion: Always use WHERE in UPDATE/DELETE. Enable SQL_SAFE_UPDATES mode to prevent accidental full-table modifications.
fix_example: UPDATE policy_data SET is_reviewed = 1 WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' AND created_date < '2023-01-01';

query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM policy_data
problem: COUNT(*) without filter scans entire table
root_cause: Full count on 10M rows. InnoDB does not store row count natively — must scan to count.
suggestion: Add a filter if you need subset count. For total count, cache the value or use approximate count via SHOW TABLE STATUS.
fix_example: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM policy_data WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'; -- or cache total count in a summary table

query: SELECT * FROM policy_archive WHERE year = 2022
problem: Archive table query scans 30M historical rows
root_cause: Archive table has no indexes added after initial bulk load. Year column has no index.
suggestion: Add index on year and state columns for archive table. Consider table partitioning by year.
fix_example: ALTER TABLE policy_archive ADD INDEX idx_year_state (year, state); -- then partition by RANGE(year)

query: SELECT state, SUM(premium_amount) FROM policy_data GROUP BY state
problem: Daily report does full table scan for aggregation
root_cause: No covering index for (state, premium_amount). Full scan needed to group all rows.
suggestion: Create a materialized summary table updated nightly. Or add covering index on (state, premium_amount).
fix_example: CREATE INDEX idx_state_premium ON policy_data (state, premium_amount); -- or use a nightly summary table

query: SELECT * FROM policy_data, agents WHERE agents.region = 'South'
problem: Cartesian product creates billions of row combinations
root_cause: Missing ON clause in join. 10M policy rows × 500 agent rows = 5 billion combinations scanned.
suggestion: Always specify JOIN ... ON condition. Use EXPLAIN to catch cartesian joins before running in production.
fix_example: SELECT p.*, a.agent_name FROM policy_data p JOIN agents a ON p.agent_id = a.id WHERE a.region = 'South';

query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE JSON_EXTRACT(data, '$.policy.state') = 'CA'
problem: JSON field filtering without functional index causes full scan
root_cause: JSON_EXTRACT() on every row is expensive. No index on JSON path. DB parses JSON for each of 10M rows.
suggestion: Create a generated/virtual column for the JSON path, then index it. MySQL 5.7+ supports functional indexes.
fix_example: ALTER TABLE policy_data ADD COLUMN state VARCHAR(2) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(data,'$.policy.state'))) VIRTUAL; CREATE INDEX idx_state ON policy_data(state);

query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE YEAR(created_date) = 2024
problem: Wrapping column in YEAR() function prevents index use
root_cause: Any function applied to an indexed column breaks the index. MySQL cannot use B-tree index on transformed values.
suggestion: Rewrite to use range condition on the raw column instead of wrapping in a function.
fix_example: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE created_date >= '2024-01-01' AND created_date < '2025-01-01';

query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE state = 'CA' OR premium_amount > 5000
problem: OR between two columns prevents efficient index usage
root_cause: MySQL cannot use a single composite index for OR across different columns. Falls back to full scan or expensive index merge.
suggestion: Rewrite as UNION of two indexed queries. Each part can use its own index efficiently.
fix_example: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE state = 'CA' UNION SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE premium_amount > 5000;

query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE policy_holder_name LIKE '%Smith%'
problem: Leading wildcard in LIKE disables B-tree index entirely
root_cause: B-tree index works left-to-right. A leading % means any prefix is valid — index cannot be used. Full scan required.
suggestion: Use FULLTEXT index for contains-style searches. Or use Elasticsearch/Opensearch for text search at scale.
fix_example: ALTER TABLE policy_data ADD FULLTEXT INDEX ft_holder_name (policy_holder_name); SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE MATCH(policy_holder_name) AGAINST('Smith');

query: SELECT * FROM claims_data WHERE policy_id = 12345
problem: Foreign key column has no index, causing full scan on lookup
root_cause: MySQL does not automatically create indexes on foreign key columns (unlike PostgreSQL). Full scan for each lookup.
suggestion: Add index on policy_id in claims_data. Always index FK columns that appear in JOIN or WHERE conditions.
fix_example: CREATE INDEX idx_claims_policy_id ON claims_data (policy_id);

query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE is_active = 1
problem: Index on low-cardinality boolean column is inefficient
root_cause: is_active has only 2 values. Index selectivity is ~50%. MySQL optimizer chooses full scan over index when selectivity < 30%.
suggestion: Create partial index or composite index. Add more selective column to the index.
fix_example: CREATE INDEX idx_active_state ON policy_data (is_active, state, created_date); -- composite improves selectivity

case_name: Index not used due to implicit type cast
query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE policy_id = '10045'
problem: Implicit type conversion prevents index use
root_cause: policy_id is INT but query passes string '10045'. MySQL applies CAST on every row to compare — breaks index.
suggestion: Match data types exactly in queries. Use integer 10045 not string '10045' for INT columns.
fix_example: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE policy_id = 10045; -- no quotes for INT column

case_name: Index not covering — causes key lookup
query: SELECT policy_id, premium_amount, agent_name FROM policy_data WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'
problem: Index exists but is not covering — causes expensive key lookup back to table
root_cause: Index on status exists but agent_name is not in the index. MySQL must go back to table for each matched row (key lookup).
suggestion: Create a covering index that includes all columns needed by the query.
fix_example: CREATE INDEX idx_status_covering ON policy_data (status, policy_id, premium_amount, agent_name);

query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE status = 'PENDING'
problem: Optimizer picks wrong plan due to outdated table statistics
root_cause: Statistics say 100 PENDING rows but there are 5M. Optimizer chooses wrong index. Run ANALYZE TABLE to refresh.
suggestion: Run ANALYZE TABLE to update statistics. Enable innodb_stats_auto_recalc. Schedule periodic ANALYZE on large tables.
fix_example: ANALYZE TABLE policy_data; -- then re-run query to verify plan with EXPLAIN

query: SELECT * FROM policy_data ORDER BY created_date DESC LIMIT 20 OFFSET 100000
problem: OFFSET 100000 forces DB to scan and discard 100k rows
root_cause: OFFSET is not a skip — MySQL reads and discards all preceding rows. Gets worse with each page.
suggestion: Use keyset/cursor-based pagination instead of OFFSET. Track last seen ID or created_date.
fix_example: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE created_date < '2024-03-15 10:22:00' ORDER BY created_date DESC LIMIT 20; -- keyset pagination

query: SELECT p.*, c.claim_amount FROM policy_data p JOIN claims_data c ON p.policy_id = c.policy_id WHERE JSON_TABLE(...)
problem: JOIN with JSON_TABLE extraction is extremely slow
root_cause: JSON_TABLE parses JSON for every joined row. No composite index on join columns. Result set is huge.
suggestion: Pre-extract JSON into relational columns. Add composite index on join columns. Filter before joining.
fix_example: -- Pre-extract JSON to a relational column, add index, then join on that column

query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE id = ?  -- called 10000 times in a loop
problem: N+1 query pattern — one query per record in a loop
root_cause: Application fetches list then queries DB for each item individually. 1 list query + N detail queries = N+1 total.
suggestion: Replace loop queries with a single JOIN or WHERE IN query. Use eager loading in ORM.
fix_example: SELECT p.*, c.claim_amount FROM policy_data p LEFT JOIN claims_data c ON p.policy_id = c.policy_id WHERE p.id IN (1,2,...,10000);

case_name: Three-table join — missing indexes on join cols
query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM policy_data p JOIN claims_data c ON p.policy_id = c.policy_id JOIN agents a ON p.agent_id = a.id
problem: Three-table join with missing indexes on join columns
root_cause: agent_id in policy_data has no index. MySQL uses nested loop join. Each row in outer table does a full scan of inner.
suggestion: Index all join columns. Use EXPLAIN to check join order and type. Consider reducing to fewer joins.
fix_example: CREATE INDEX idx_policy_agent_id ON policy_data (agent_id); CREATE INDEX idx_claims_policy_id ON claims_data (policy_id);

query: SELECT a.policy_id FROM policy_data a JOIN policy_data b ON a.agent_id = b.agent_id WHERE b.state = 'TX'
problem: Self-join on 10M row table is very expensive
root_cause: Self-join multiplies row combinations. Without tight indexes, creates massive intermediate result set.
suggestion: Rewrite using subquery or CTE. Index the join columns. Filter aggressively before the join.
fix_example: WITH tx_agents AS (SELECT DISTINCT agent_id FROM policy_data WHERE state = 'TX') SELECT policy_id FROM policy_data WHERE agent_id IN (SELECT agent_id FROM tx_agents);

query: SELECT * FROM policy_data p JOIN audit_log a ON p.policy_id = a.policy_id
problem: JOIN between two large tables produces massive intermediate result set
root_cause: policy_data (10M) × audit_log (500M) = potentially billions of intermediate rows. Spills to disk.
suggestion: Always filter before joining. Never join two large tables without reducing rows first via WHERE.
fix_example: SELECT p.policy_id, a.action FROM policy_data p JOIN audit_log a ON p.policy_id = a.policy_id WHERE p.state = 'CA' AND a.created_date > '2024-01-01';

query: SELECT p.state, r.rate FROM policy_data p CROSS JOIN rate_table r
problem: CROSS JOIN multiplies every row with every other row
root_cause: CROSS JOIN between 10M policies and 500 rates = 5 billion rows. Usually a mistake.
suggestion: Replace CROSS JOIN with INNER JOIN on a matching column. If intentional, filter results heavily.
fix_example: SELECT p.state, r.rate FROM policy_data p INNER JOIN rate_table r ON p.rate_class = r.rate_class;

case_name: Subquery in SELECT for each row
query: SELECT policy_id, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM claims_data c WHERE c.policy_id = p.policy_id) AS claim_count FROM policy_data p
problem: Correlated subquery in SELECT runs once per outer row
root_cause: For each of 10M policies, one COUNT query fires on claims_data. 10M individual queries = extremely slow.
suggestion: Replace correlated subquery with a LEFT JOIN + GROUP BY. Runs in a single pass.
fix_example: SELECT p.policy_id, COUNT(c.claim_id) AS claim_count FROM policy_data p LEFT JOIN claims_data c ON p.policy_id = c.policy_id GROUP BY p.policy_id;

query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE policy_id IN (SELECT policy_id FROM claims_data WHERE claim_amount > 5000)
problem: IN with subquery can trigger row-by-row evaluation
root_cause: Depending on MySQL version, IN subquery may run per outer row. No index on claim_amount.
suggestion: Rewrite as JOIN or EXISTS. Add index on claim_amount. JOIN is almost always faster than IN subquery.
fix_example: SELECT DISTINCT p.* FROM policy_data p JOIN claims_data c ON p.policy_id = c.policy_id WHERE c.claim_amount > 5000;

query: SELECT policy_id, premium_amount FROM policy_data WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'
problem: Query that was 1 sec is suddenly taking 50 seconds
root_cause: Possible causes: table lock from another query, index fragmentation, sudden data volume spike, or missing statistics after bulk insert.
suggestion: Run SHOW PROCESSLIST to check locks. Run EXPLAIN to verify plan still uses index. Run ANALYZE TABLE. Check if bulk data was recently inserted.
fix_example: SHOW PROCESSLIST; EXPLAIN SELECT policy_id, premium_amount FROM policy_data WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'; ANALYZE TABLE policy_data;

query: UPDATE claims_data SET status = 'PROCESSED' WHERE claim_id = ?
problem: Deadlock between two concurrent transactions causes retries and latency
root_cause: Transaction A locks claim row 1 then row 2. Transaction B locks row 2 then row 1. MySQL detects cycle and kills one.
suggestion: Always access rows in consistent order. Keep transactions short. Use SELECT ... FOR UPDATE to pre-lock. Implement retry logic.
fix_example: -- Access rows in same order in all transactions. Use: SELECT * FROM claims_data WHERE claim_id = ? FOR UPDATE; -- then UPDATE

query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE agent_id = ?
problem: All DB connections are in use — queries queue up and time out
root_cause: Connection pool max (e.g. 100) reached. New requests wait. Could be a slow query holding connections open too long.
suggestion: Increase pool size carefully. Fix the slow query holding connections. Implement connection timeout. Use connection pooler like PgBouncer/ProxySQL.
fix_example: -- In app config: increase pool_size. Add query timeout. Monitor with: SHOW STATUS LIKE 'Threads_connected';

case_name: Memory pressure — sort spilling to disk
query: SELECT * FROM policy_data ORDER BY premium_amount DESC
problem: Large sort operation overflows memory and spills to disk
root_cause: EXPLAIN shows 'Using filesort'. sort_buffer_size too small for 10M row result. Disk I/O crushes performance.
suggestion: Add index on sort column. Increase sort_buffer_size. Always add WHERE to reduce rows before sorting.
fix_example: CREATE INDEX idx_premium ON policy_data (premium_amount DESC); SELECT policy_id, premium_amount FROM policy_data WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' ORDER BY premium_amount DESC LIMIT 100;

query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE policy_id = 99999
problem: Read replica is lagging — queries return outdated data
root_cause: Replication lag between primary and replica. App reads from replica that is 30 seconds behind. Shows old records.
suggestion: Route critical reads to primary. Monitor replication lag with Seconds_Behind_Master. Use semi-sync replication.
fix_example: SHOW SLAVE STATUS; -- check Seconds_Behind_Master. Route time-sensitive reads to primary DB.

query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'
problem: All queries on table frozen during ALTER TABLE operation
root_cause: ALTER TABLE acquires metadata lock. All reads and writes queue until ALTER completes. Can block for hours on large tables.
suggestion: Use pt-online-schema-change or gh-ost for zero-downtime schema changes. Schedule ALTER in maintenance window.
fix_example: -- Use: pt-online-schema-change --alter 'ADD COLUMN new_field INT' D=mydb,t=policy_data --execute

query: SELECT * FROM audit_log WHERE event_type = 'LOGIN' ORDER BY created_date DESC LIMIT 1000
problem: Query slow due to disk I/O saturation on audit_log table
root_cause: 500M row audit_log with high write rate saturates disk IOPS. Reads compete with writes for I/O bandwidth.
suggestion: Move audit_log to separate storage. Add SSD. Partition table by date. Archive old data regularly.
fix_example: -- Partition audit_log by RANGE on YEAR(created_date). Archive partitions older than 90 days.

case_name: CPU spike from regex in query
query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE policy_holder_name REGEXP '^[A-Z][a-z]+ [A-Z]'
problem: REGEXP causes high CPU usage and full scan
root_cause: REGEXP cannot use indexes. Evaluates regex engine for every row. Complex regex is CPU-intensive.
suggestion: Use FULLTEXT index for name searches. Or pre-validate names at insert time. Avoid REGEXP in WHERE on large tables.
fix_example: -- Add FULLTEXT index and use MATCH AGAINST. Or validate/normalize names at write time.

case_name: High frequency config lookup — no cache
query: SELECT config_value FROM system_config WHERE module = ? AND key = ?
problem: Ultra-fast query called 100k times/hour saturates DB despite being quick
root_cause: Config data changes once a day but is queried 100k/hour. No caching. DB CPU wasted on repetitive identical queries.
suggestion: Cache config in Redis with TTL of 5 minutes. Or load all config at app startup into memory. Reduces 100k DB hits to near zero.
fix_example: # Python: cache = redis.get(f'config:{module}:{key}') or db.query() then redis.setex(key, 300, value)

query: SELECT * FROM config_table WHERE key = ?
problem: Individually fast query overwhelms DB through sheer frequency
root_cause: 50k queries/hour = 14/second continuous. Each one is cheap, but combined they consume significant DB thread pool.
suggestion: Introduce Redis cache. Use application-level in-memory cache (LRU). Batch similar lookups into one query.
fix_example: # Use @lru_cache or Redis. Batch: SELECT key, value FROM config_table WHERE key IN ('k1','k2','k3',...)

case_name: Same query run by 1000 concurrent users
query: SELECT * FROM premium_rate_table WHERE state = ? AND coverage_type = ?
problem: 1000 users hitting the same query simultaneously — thundering herd
root_cause: All 1000 requests miss cache simultaneously (cache stampede). Each fires same DB query. DB connection pool maxed out.
suggestion: Use Redis cache with lock (mutex). Only one request fetches from DB, others wait for cache. Add query result cache at DB level.
fix_example: # Use cache lock pattern: if not cache.get(key): with lock: if not cache.get(key): cache.set(key, db.query())

case_name: Rate table queried per policy transaction
query: SELECT rate FROM rate_table WHERE state = ? AND class = ?
problem: Rate table queried for every single insurance transaction
root_cause: 500k daily transactions each trigger a rate lookup. Rate table has ~1000 rows — ideal for full in-memory cache.
suggestion: Load entire rate_table into application memory at startup. Refresh every 30 minutes. Eliminates 500k daily DB round trips.
fix_example: # At startup: rate_cache = {(row.state, row.class): row.rate for row in db.query('SELECT * FROM rate_table')}

query: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(premium_amount) FROM policy_data WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'
problem: Heavy aggregation query triggered every 5 seconds by dashboard auto-refresh
root_cause: 8-second query fired every 5 seconds means it never completes before next one starts. Queries pile up.
suggestion: Cache dashboard metrics in Redis. Refresh cache every 60 seconds via a background job. Serve stale-while-revalidate.
fix_example: # Background job every 60s: redis.set('dashboard:active_policies', db.query(...), ex=120)

case_name: Health check endpoint queries DB every second
query: SELECT 1 FROM policy_data LIMIT 1
problem: Load balancer health check pings DB every second unnecessarily
root_cause: SELECT 1 is cheap but from 10 servers × 1/sec = 600 connection open/close cycles per minute. Wastes connections.
suggestion: Health check should only verify DB connection is open, not query. Or cache health status for 10 seconds.
fix_example: # In health check: just verify connection pool has live connection. Don't execute a query.

query: SELECT * FROM audit_log WHERE created_date > '2024-01-01'
problem: 500M row audit table with no partitioning — even date-filtered queries scan too much
root_cause: Without partitioning, index on created_date still reads from a monolithic 500M row table. Index overhead is huge.
suggestion: Partition audit_log by RANGE on YEAR(created_date). Each year is ~50M rows. Date queries touch only relevant partition.
fix_example: ALTER TABLE audit_log PARTITION BY RANGE (YEAR(created_date)) (PARTITION p2022 VALUES LESS THAN (2023), PARTITION p2023 VALUES LESS THAN (2024), ...)

case_name: Storing JSON where relational columns needed
query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE JSON_EXTRACT(data, '$.coverage.type') = 'AUTO'
problem: Structured data stored as JSON prevents efficient indexing
root_cause: Frequently-queried fields like coverage_type stored in JSON blob. Cannot be directly indexed. Full scan + JSON parse.
suggestion: Extract frequently queried JSON fields into regular columns with indexes. Keep JSON only for truly unstructured data.
fix_example: ALTER TABLE policy_data ADD COLUMN coverage_type VARCHAR(20); UPDATE policy_data SET coverage_type = JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(data,'$.coverage.type')); CREATE INDEX idx_coverage_type ON policy_data(coverage_type);

query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE premium_amount > '1000'
problem: Numeric column stored as VARCHAR causes wrong sort order and slow comparisons
root_cause: VARCHAR comparison is lexicographic: '9' > '10000'. Index on VARCHAR numeric is wrong. Type cast on every row.
suggestion: Change column type to DECIMAL(10,2) for monetary values. Never store numbers as strings.
fix_example: ALTER TABLE policy_data MODIFY COLUMN premium_amount DECIMAL(10,2); CREATE INDEX idx_premium ON policy_data(premium_amount);

case_name: Missing composite index for common query pattern
query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE state = 'CA' AND status = 'ACTIVE' AND created_date > '2024-01-01'
problem: Common 3-column filter pattern has no composite index
root_cause: Separate indexes exist on state, status, created_date individually. MySQL can only use one at a time for this pattern.
suggestion: Create composite index in the order of: most selective first, then range column last.
fix_example: CREATE INDEX idx_state_status_date ON policy_data (state, status, created_date); -- status first if more selective

query: INSERT INTO policy_data VALUES (...)
problem: Table has 15 indexes — all must be updated on every INSERT/UPDATE
root_cause: Each index is a B-tree that must be updated on write. 15 indexes = 15 separate write operations per row insert.
suggestion: Audit indexes. Remove unused ones (check with sys.schema_unused_indexes). Keep only what queries actually use.
fix_example: SELECT * FROM sys.schema_unused_indexes WHERE object_schema = 'your_db'; -- drop unused indexes

query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE status = 'CANCELLED'
problem: Table grows indefinitely without archiving — all queries slow over time
root_cause: Cancelled policies (60% of table) never purged. Table size doubles every 2 years. Index maintenance gets slower.
suggestion: Archive records older than 2 years to policy_archive table. Run periodic purge job. Use partitioning for easy drops.
fix_example: INSERT INTO policy_archive SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE status='CANCELLED' AND created_date < NOW() - INTERVAL 2 YEAR; DELETE FROM policy_data WHERE status='CANCELLED' AND created_date < NOW() - INTERVAL 2 YEAR;

case_name: ENUM type causing ALTER TABLE pain
query: ALTER TABLE policy_data MODIFY COLUMN status ENUM('ACTIVE','CANCELLED','EXPIRED','PENDING','RENEWED')
problem: Adding new value to ENUM requires full table rebuild in older MySQL versions
root_cause: Pre-MySQL 5.7: any ENUM change requires full table copy. 10M rows = very long ALTER with table lock.
suggestion: Use VARCHAR with CHECK constraint or a separate status lookup table instead of ENUM. Easier to extend.
fix_example: ALTER TABLE policy_data MODIFY COLUMN status VARCHAR(20); CREATE INDEX idx_status ON policy_data(status);

case_name: Missing created_date index on time-series queries
query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE created_date BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2024-03-31'
problem: Date range queries scan too many rows due to missing index
root_cause: No index on created_date. Date range must scan entire table to find qualifying rows.
suggestion: Add index on created_date. For very large tables, combine with partitioning by date range.
fix_example: CREATE INDEX idx_created_date ON policy_data (created_date); -- query will now use index range scan

query: UPDATE policy_data SET status = 'EXPIRED' WHERE expiry_date < NOW()
problem: Daily batch UPDATE locks table and runs slowly without index
root_cause: No index on expiry_date. Full scan to find expiring policies. Table-level lock during 2M row update.
suggestion: Add index on expiry_date. Process in batches of 10k rows. Run during off-peak hours.
fix_example: CREATE INDEX idx_expiry_date ON policy_data (expiry_date); -- then batch update: UPDATE policy_data SET status='EXPIRED' WHERE expiry_date < NOW() LIMIT 10000; -- loop

query: INSERT INTO policy_data SELECT * FROM policy_staging
problem: Nightly bulk insert from staging locks policy_data for 5 minutes
root_cause: Single INSERT ... SELECT statement locks entire table. All reads blocked during insert. Indexes rebuilt at end.
suggestion: Use LOAD DATA INFILE for bulk inserts. Insert in batches of 1000. Disable indexes during insert then rebuild.
fix_example: LOAD DATA INFILE '/tmp/policies.csv' INTO TABLE policy_data; -- or insert in 1000-row batches with index disable

case_name: Auto-increment bottleneck on high write rate
query: INSERT INTO policy_data (policy_holder_name, ...) VALUES (...)
problem: AUTO_INCREMENT mutex becomes bottleneck at 10k inserts/second
root_cause: InnoDB AUTO_INCREMENT uses a table-level mutex. High-rate inserts serialize on this lock.
suggestion: Set innodb_autoinc_lock_mode=2. Use UUID or application-generated IDs for very high write rates. Use batched inserts.
fix_example: SET GLOBAL innodb_autoinc_lock_mode = 2; -- or use INSERT INTO ... VALUES (...),(...),(...) for batching

query: UPDATE policy_data SET premium_amount = premium_amount * 1.05 WHERE state = 'CA'
problem: Mass UPDATE causes index fragmentation and degrades future query performance
root_cause: Updating premium_amount for 2M CA rows fragments the B-tree index. Subsequent queries slower due to fragmented index pages.
suggestion: Run OPTIMIZE TABLE after large updates. Schedule during maintenance window. Monitor index fragmentation.
fix_example: OPTIMIZE TABLE policy_data; -- or ALTER TABLE policy_data ENGINE=InnoDB; -- to rebuild indexes

case_name: DELETE without index causes full scan
query: DELETE FROM audit_log WHERE created_date < '2022-01-01'
problem: Monthly data purge DELETE runs for 4 minutes without index
root_cause: No index on created_date in audit_log. Full scan to find rows older than 2 years. Locks table during scan.
suggestion: Add index on created_date. Delete in batches. Use partitioning — drop entire partition instead of row-by-row delete.
fix_example: -- With partitioning: ALTER TABLE audit_log DROP PARTITION p2021; -- instant, no row-by-row delete needed

case_name: Concurrent UPDATEs on same rows cause contention
query: UPDATE policy_data SET view_count = view_count + 1 WHERE policy_id = ?
problem: High-concurrency counter UPDATE creates row-level lock contention on hot rows
root_cause: Many threads updating the same row's view_count. Each must wait for the row lock to release.
suggestion: Use Redis for real-time counters. Batch DB updates every minute. Or use INSERT into a counter log table and SUM later.
fix_example: # Redis: redis.incr(f'policy:view:{policy_id}') -- sync to DB in batches every 60s

query: -- All queries slower than expected despite good indexes
problem: InnoDB buffer pool too small — data not cached in memory
root_cause: Buffer pool set to 128MB on a server with 64GB RAM. All data reads go to disk instead of memory. 100x slower.
suggestion: Set innodb_buffer_pool_size to 70-80% of available RAM. Monitor buffer pool hit ratio — should be >99%.
fix_example: SET GLOBAL innodb_buffer_pool_size = 48*1024*1024*1024; -- 48GB for a 64GB server

query: -- All write-heavy queries slower, reads not improving
problem: MySQL query cache causing global mutex contention on write-heavy workload
root_cause: Query cache uses a global lock. On write-heavy tables, cache is constantly invalidated. Lock contention worse than no cache.
suggestion: Disable MySQL query cache (deprecated in MySQL 8). Use Redis/Memcached at application layer instead.
fix_example: SET GLOBAL query_cache_size = 0; SET GLOBAL query_cache_type = 0; -- Use application-level caching

query: -- Error: Too many connections
problem: max_connections limit hit during peak load — new connections rejected
root_cause: max_connections = 100 but app has 20 servers each with pool of 50 = 1000 potential connections. Overflow rejected.
suggestion: Increase max_connections. Use a connection pooler (ProxySQL, PgBouncer). Reduce per-server pool size.
fix_example: SET GLOBAL max_connections = 500; -- also add ProxySQL between app and DB for connection multiplexing

query: -- Cannot identify which queries are slow
problem: No slow query logging — cannot identify performance bottlenecks
root_cause: slow_query_log disabled. No visibility into which queries exceed threshold. Performance degradation is invisible.
suggestion: Enable slow_query_log with long_query_time=1. Use pt-query-digest to analyze patterns. Set up Percona Monitoring.
fix_example: SET GLOBAL slow_query_log = 1; SET GLOBAL long_query_time = 1; SET GLOBAL slow_query_log_file = '/var/log/mysql/slow.log';

query: SELECT * FROM policy_data WHERE state = 'CA'
problem: All reads and writes going to primary DB — replicas unused
root_cause: App does not implement read/write splitting. Primary handles 100% of load. Replicas are idle standbys.
suggestion: Route SELECT queries to read replicas. Use ProxySQL or application-level routing. Primary handles writes only.
fix_example: # In app config: read_db = replica_host, write_db = primary_host. Or use ProxySQL rules for auto-routing.

query: INSERT INTO policy_data VALUES (...) -- write throughput low
problem: Write performance limited by overly conservative innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit=1
root_cause: Setting=1 means fsync on every commit. On HDD this is ~150 writes/sec max. SSD helps but setting=2 is much faster.
suggestion: Set to 2 for most workloads (flush per second, not per commit). Set to 0 for max performance if data loss risk is acceptable.
fix_example: SET GLOBAL innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit = 2; -- flushes every 1 second, loses max 1 second of data on crash
